chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Tatum days: Murray McEachern, Ed Fant and the Goodman hire
summary: At the Three Deuces trombonist Murray McEachern broke into the checkroom to play after hearing Ed Fant, and Goodman hired him; Collins also met Dorsey band members.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Thank you, thank you, that's reassuring. Now we'll talk about Art.
I won't talk about me any more. I'll just --
I'm going to talk about Art Tatum when Scoops Carey worked with Art Tatum and John Collins was there also, you know.
Although it was a well-kept secret.
That's right, you know. I wasn't

supposed to be there but I was there and I'll tell you about the time Murray McEachern came to the Three Deuces and he wanted to hear Art, and he just got in from Canada and he was afraid to bring his trombone in so he checked his trombone in the check room and came in. And at this time we had a guy sitting in with us who played with Earl Hines. His name was Ed Fant. And he was a trombone player. And Murray heard -- this is a black guy, Eddie Fant, and Murray heard Fant play and he broke that checkroom door down getting his trombone, and coming up and playing. And he amazed all of us, including Fant.

So consequently Benny Goodman heard him playing down there because he used to come very night, and this is how Benny Goodman hired him, and this is why he hired him. He heard him at the Three Deuces. Benny was playing at the Congress Hotel then, I believe. Yes, and this is how I first met Murray McEachern. See, I think Murray can attest to the fact that I exist, you know, we played together then --

You know. Ask Allen Russ Rules, you know, he -- you know, we were friends then, in Chicago, and also there at that time -- after Benny left I think it was Jimmy Dorsey and this is -- with Roy we used to go and do concerts on Sunday afternoons at the Congress Hotel, and Jimmy's band was there, and this is how I met Shorty Sherock Toots Camarata, Tuss Camarada, you know. They were in the band at this time. So I do exist.
